headline: New York State Land Use and Trailhead Permits
reservation: Most Adirondack hiking does not require a reservation, but access rules vary by land manager. Adirondack Mountain Reserve access requires advance reservations during its posted season; developed DEC campgrounds use a separate booking system. Check the specific trailhead and campground rules before travel.

days.title: Olympic Legacy and Lakes
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Lake Placid Village

stops.name: Mirror Lake
stops.detail: Walk the paved path around Mirror Lake for reflections of the High Peaks. Check a current local map for the route distance.

stops.name: Olympic Jumping Complex
stops.detail: Visit the skydeck of the jumping towers for a view over the Ausable River valley.

days.driving: Minimal; local transfers within Lake Placid are short, but parking in the village is limited.
days.note: Check seasonal operating hours for Olympic venues as they vary significantly between summer and winter.

days.title: High Peaks Perspectives
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Heart Lake Trailhead

stops.name: Mount Jo
stops.detail: Hike the steep, rocky trail for an overlook of Heart Lake and the MacIntyre Range.

stops.name: Whiteface Veterans' Memorial Highway
stops.detail: Drive the historic toll road to the summit area for 360-degree views of the Adirondack Park.

days.driving: Allow extra time for the Mount Jo hike, transfer to Whiteface and summit-road visit; treat them as separate outings if needed.
days.note: Prepare for significant temperature drops and high winds at mountain summits.

days.title: Interconnected Waterways

stops.name: Lower Saranac Lake
stops.detail: Explore the shoreline or islands by canoe or kayak, following local navigation markers.

stops.name: The Wild Center
stops.detail: Visit the natural history museum in Tupper Lake for the elevated Wild Walk through the treetops.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the circuit between Saranac Lake and Tupper Lake; conditions vary.
days.note: Always wear a PFD when on the water; mountain lakes can become rough quickly in wind.

intel.title: High Peaks Trailhead Demand
intel.text: Popular lots like the Adirondak Loj often fill before dawn on summer weekends. Use local hiker shuttles when operating or choose lower-elevation trails to avoid congestion.

intel.title: Vast Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is unavailable in most of the backcountry and along many stretches of Route 3 and 30. Ensure you have physical maps and have shared your itinerary with someone before heading out.

intel.title: Village Hub Supplies
intel.text: Fuel and groceries are readily available in Lake Placid, Saranac Lake, and Tupper Lake. Plan ahead when driving south toward Long Lake where services are more infrequent.

intel.title: Mud Season Constraints
intel.text: In spring, check DEC advisories before choosing High Peaks routes. During unstable conditions, DEC may recommend avoiding high-elevation trails because of snow, ice, mud and erosion risk.

intel.title: Public-Private Boundaries
intel.text: The park is a 'blue line' boundary containing private towns and public forest. Respect all 'Posted' signs on private land and stay on designated state-maintained trails.

plan.arrival: Landing at SLK involves a 15-minute drive to Saranac Lake. Use the first few hours to check weather forecasts at the visitor center and confirm your gear for the terrain.
plan.vehicle: A standard vehicle is fine for paved routes; high-clearance is recommended for certain unpaved state-truck trails. Check rental terms for dirt road travel.
plan.goldenHour: Mount Van Hoevenberg offers clear views of the High Peaks at dusk; trail conditions vary seasonally.
